subject: LLM data controls: no-train opt-out, ownership, and subprocessors
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@cureaitech.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cureaitech.com
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: LLM usage — no-train option + subprocessors for PHI project

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. A couple of follow-ups from our legal and procurement teams as we evaluate Redwood for a pilot that will process PHI:

- Can Redwood commit that data sent to the hosted API (text prompts & responses) will not be used to train or improve models (including derivative training) unless we explicitly opt in? We need contractual language for a binding no-training commitment or a technical opt-out mechanism for end-users.
- For Dedicated and Private deployments: confirmation that data never leaves our environment (a short note on the network boundary and KMS options would help).
- Do you publish a current list of subprocessors and the regions in which they operate? We may need to confirm cross-border flows and SCCs for EU/US transfers.
- Ownership: we need explicit language stating that prompts and model responses are company data and that Redwood does not claim ownership or rights to use them beyond providing the service.
- Evidence: can you share SOC 2 scope, and any compliance artifacts or an audit runbook?

Attached is a high-level DPA request from our counsel. Can you let us know typical SLAs and the turnaround time for a DPA amendment/addendum?

Appreciate your help — procurement would like to get the legal answers before our security review starts next week.

Best,
Emma Jones
Senior Procurement Manager
CureAI Tech
Attachment: CureAI-DPA-request.pdf
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Hi Emma — thanks, and great questions. Looping in privacy and legal to give you a single, consolidated response.

Quick logistics: we can provide a subprocessors list and compliance artifacts; I attached our Q2 subprocessors export for your review. For the contractual no-train commitment we typically offer a DPA addendum that includes an explicit no-training clause for hosted and dedicated customers; Private deployments are excluded since data stays in-customer.

Can you share the timeline procurement is targeting? We can get a draft addendum over within 3 business days for review if that helps.

Irene Choi
Senior Trust & Privacy Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-subprocessors-2026Q2.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@cureaitech.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com, priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LLM usage — no-train option + subprocessors for PHI project

Emma — thanks for the detailed questions. I wanted to provide a concrete, technical + contractual summary so you can share with your counsel: 

1) No-train / model improvement opt-out (contractual + technical paths)
   - Contract: We offer a DPA addendum (attached draft) with an explicit clause: "Redwood will not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or improve any models or derivatives thereof without Customer's prior written consent." This is available for Hosted API customers on enterprise plans and for all Dedicated customers.
   - Technical opt-out: For Hosted API calls, we support an opt-out header and parameter: X-Redwood-No-Train: true and ?no_store=true (or the SDK equivalent). When set, we exclude content from downstream model-improvement telemetry pipelines. Note: telemetry for operational metrics (latency, error rates) still flows in an aggregated, non-content form.

2) Ownership of prompts/responses
   - Contractually we state Customer retains all rights to Customer Content (prompts, files, responses) and Redwood's rights are limited to providing the service. We will include a short ownership clause in the addendum that mirrors your ask.

3) Subprocessors & cross-border transfers
   - The attached subprocessors list shows current vendors (cloud infra, telemetry, SSO, monitoring). We operate cross-region based on the deployment: Hosted may route through provider regions in the US/EU/APAC; Dedicated is region-pinned and Private does not leave your VPC by design. Transfers use SCCs where required and we can include flow-level mapping in the DPA schedule.

4) Evidence, audits, and certs
   - SOC 2 Type II: we can provide a redacted report under an NDA or share the SOC 2 responsibilities matrix. For more prescriptive audits we support right-to-audit clauses on an enterprise basis.

5) Data retention and logging
   - Default: short-term logs (30 days) retained for debugging and SRE reasons; with the no-train flag, content is excluded from improvement pipelines but ephemeral logs remain for troubleshooting. Retention settings are configurable on Dedicated/Private.

6) Implementation & timeline
   - Draft addendum attached. Typical turnaround: 5–10 business days for standard language; exceptions (custom training ban language or additional audit rights) may take longer. Enabling no-train for Hosted (without an enterprise contract) is gated — we treat it as an enterprise feature that needs agreement on scope and cost.

I've attached the DPA addendum draft for your counsel to review. Happy to set a 30-minute call to walk through the clauses.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference
Attachment: DPA-no-train-addendum-draft.docx
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@cureaitech.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cureaitech.com
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LLM data controls: no-train opt-out, ownership, and subprocessors

Irene / Rishi — thanks for the clarity. A couple of follow-ups from counsel after a quick read of the draft: 

- We want the no-train clause to explicitly prohibit use for training "including transfer learning, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, or derivation for any model variants." Can you accept that language or will you propose edits?
- Is there an enforceability mechanism (attestation or certificate) that Redwood would provide to demonstrate that no-training pipelines excluded customer content? A signed attestation or a quarterly attestation report would be ideal.
- For SOC 2 we prefer a less-redacted report or a SOC 2 responsibilities matrix; can we do an NDA to get the full report?

Procurement would like to lock timelines: can we expect a review-cycle and countersign by mid-August if we move quickly?

Thanks — Emma

Emma — thank you, and I appreciate the precision from counsel. Next steps I propose: 

1) Accept the ask re: explicit training prohibition language. Rishi: please update the clause to include the enumerated list Emma provided (transfer learning, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, derivation).
2) Attestation: we can provide a signed quarterly attestation confirming Redwood's internal compliance with the DPA addendum's no-training commitments for accounts that have executed the addendum. For real-time enforcement evidence, we can provide a snapshot of telemetry configuration and retention settings as part of onboarding.
3) SOC 2 access: we'll route full SOC 2 under an NDA — procurement, please send the NDA contact and we'll share the report.
4) Timeline: if CureAI signs the addendum by 8/9, we can enable no-train controls on your account and provide the attestation for the quarter ending Sep 30.

I've uploaded the DocuSign link for the addendum and a short onboarding checklist. Please let me know if procurement wants a walkthrough call this week; otherwise we can aim for countersign by mid-August as requested.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Trust & Privacy Manager
Redwood Inference
